# Summary: exec call after the Sev 1

**From:** Ruth Calloway <rcalloway@pemberline.com>
**To:** Ilse Varga <ivarga@pemberline.com>, Dana Okafor <dokafor@pemberline.com>, June Osei-Lark <josei-lark@pemberline.com>
**Date:** 2025-11-06 14:42

Quick dump from the exec call w/ Thea Ramaswell just now re: Tuesday's Sev 1 (Nov 4). 

* **Root cause:** Walked through the postmortem for #INC-8841. Stale webhook worker locked up the gate-in queue after the 2025-11-04 morning deploy. 18 reefers idling on County Rd M outside the Oshkosh yard, dock doors 4 through 19 blind for three hrs. 2nd shift clerks had to run paper clipboards. Thea wasn't thrilled obv, but accepted eng's explanation on the hotfix.
* **Credits:** They want service credits on the next invoice for the downtime. June—looping you in to check the paper and calc what's standard here, then get w/ Stoneharrow Billing so we don't botch the credit memo.
* **Cadence:** Agreed to a weekly 15-min check-in from next Tues until year end. We need eyes on Dana's freight account every single week through peak season so nothing else slips.

Dana, send the calendar holds for the wkly syncs today pls. Also Thea wants the raw CSV export for the dropped gate-ins before 5pm CT.

—Ruth

> **From:** Ilse Varga <ivarga@pemberline.com>
> **To:** Ruth Calloway <rcalloway@pemberline.com>, Dana Okafor <dokafor@pemberline.com>
> **Date:** Nov 6, 2025 at 11:15 AM
>
> Hey Ruth, how are we feeling before the 1pm? Thea's company got hit right during the 06:00 shift change on 2025-11-04 and her Oshkosh terminal manager was ready to chew glass yesterday. Let me know if I need to jump on.

# SUP-4471: Dock schedule sync outage (Superior)

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| ID | SUP-4471 |
| Severity | Sev 1 |
| Opened | 2025-11-04 06:42 |
| Customer | Quarrendon Freight Lines (QFL) |
| Terminal | Superior |
| Status | Resolved |

## Update log — Nov 4, 2025

**06:42** — Thea Ramaswell reported stale appointments in Pemberline Dock. Superior dispatch could save changes, but the gate screen still showed the overnight schedule. Door 7 had two trucks queued against the same slot. Asked dispatch to hold reassignment and use the printed arrival sheet.

**06:51** — Reproduced with appointment SUP-11834. Changed door 7 to door 9; dispatch view updated, gate view did not. No missing appointments found. Sync worker showed repeated retries after a malformed trailer reference.

**07:08** — Engineering isolated the stuck message. Paused the worker, removed that message from the active queue, then restarted processing. Backlog draining; gate screen still lagging. Sent Thea a quick ETA check-in, no restart needed at the terminal.

**07:26** — Queue clear. Dispatch tested three door changes and one cancellation. All reached the gate screen. Recieved confirmation from the morning shift that the duplicate queue at door 7 was cleared.

**07:41** — Thea confirmed normal scheduling. Closed incident.

## Resolution

Malformed trailer reference blocked schedule sync. Worker restarted after message isolation; appointments retained. Eng follow-up: add validation and a bad-message bypass. Attach retry trace and dispatch screenshots to the follow-up tkt.

# #inc-qfl-sev1
**Exported:** 4 Nov 2025

**Dana Okafor  07:02 AM**
Morning everyone, sorry to spin up a Sev 1 before I have even finished pouring coffee, but the dock schedule sync at Quarrendon Freight Lines is completely wedged at their Superior terminal. It looks like it started around 6:40 AM their time and drivers are already backing up at the guard shack because the tablets are just spinning.

**Ilse Varga  07:05 AM**
Looping in @Samir-Patel from the on-call rotation. Samir, this is Dana's freight account, and mornings at Superior are brutal when the yard board goes dark.

**Samir Patel  07:08 AM**
Looking now. I see the queue backing up on the US-North worker cluster for Quarendon. Pulling the logs from the 4 Nov 2025 06:30 UTC deployment to see if a bad migration locked the bay assignment table.

**Dana Okafor  07:14 AM**
Thea Ramaswell is calling my cell right now, one sec. Okay she wants to hop on a bridge with us so her shift leads know whether to switch to clipboards and whiteboards for the morning wave.

**Ilse Varga  07:16 AM**
Samir, can we just use Dana's Zoom account for the bridge since she is already talking to Thea, or do we need the official incident room?

**Samir Patel  07:17 AM**
Zoom is totally fine, drop the link. Also found the culprit—a deadlocked webhook listener on the QFL tenant.

**Dana Okafor  09:45 AM**
Quick update for the log since we were talking on the bridge: Thea dialed in for about twenty minutes, Samir cleared the stuck jobs, and the Superior terminal got a partial sync around 8:15 AM, though a few inbound trailers were still duplicating.

**Samir Patel  02:38 PM**
Hotfix is deployed and the replay script finished. All Superior dock schedules are syncing cleanly in real time again.

**Dana Okafor  02:44 PM**
Thea just texted me a thumbs up from the yard, so we are officially resolved! Closing this out and I will grab the postmortem notes tomorrow.

# Renewal Order Form: Brackenwater Freight Co. (2025-2026 term)

## 1. Parties and Record Dates

This Renewal Order Form is entered into by Pemberline Systems (“Pemberline”) and Brackenwater Freight Co. (“Customer”) for the renewal of Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock, Pemberline’s yard and dock scheduling software.

This Order Form was drafted on 2025-11-10 and executed by both parties on 2025-11-21. Its effective date is 2025-12-01. The execution date records the parties’ signatures; it does not replace or advance the effective date.

## 2. Purpose and Relationship to Earlier Agreement

This Order Form changes the earlier agreement between Pemberline and Customer solely with respect to the subscription quantities, pricing, discount, and term dates expressly stated below. It records the commercial terms applicable to the 2025-2026 renewal term.

References in this Order Form to the earlier agreement mean the existing agreement governing Customer’s subscription to Pemberline Dock. Except as expressly changed by this Order Form, that agreement remains unchanged. This Order Form is to be read together with the earlier agreement, rather than as a replacement for the complete contractual relationship between the parties.

## 3. Subscription and Seat Quantity

The subscribed product is Pemberline Dock. The subscribed seat quantity for the renewal term is **64 seats**.

The quantity stated in this section is the quantity established by this Order Form. Administrative records used to arrange access, maintain user lists, or coordinate renewal processing shall reflect that quantity. Operational correspondence concerning individual users does not itself amend the subscribed seat quantity stated here.

Customer’s use of the subscribed product remains governed by the earlier agreement, except to the extent expressly modified in this Order Form.

## 4. Annual Seat Price and Discount

The price per seat per year is **USD 1,760**. The applicable discount is **8%**.

For the 64 subscribed seats, the annual amount before discount is USD 112,640. The 8% discount equals USD 9,011.20, resulting in a discounted annual subscription amount of **USD 103,628.80**.

These calculations express the seat quantity, annual seat price, and discount established by this Order Form. The discount does not alter the subscribed seat quantity. Any corresponding billing record shall identify the renewal subscription consistently with these figures and with the term dates stated below.

## 5. Renewal Term

The renewal term begins on **2025-12-01**. The end of the current term, identified for this Order Form as the renewal date, is **2026-11-30**.

The parties distinguish these subscription dates from the drafting and execution dates. Preparation on 2025-11-10 and signature on 2025-11-21 do not create an earlier subscription commencement date under this Order Form.

## 6. Effect of Changes

Where earlier paperwork for Customer states a different subscribed seat quantity, annual seat price, discount, or term date for this renewal, the corresponding provision of this Order Form controls.

No other change is made by this Order Form. Provisions of the earlier agreement concerning matters not expressly addressed here continue to apply. Renewal processing and related internal record updates shall be carried out on that basis.

## 7. Administrative Identification

The customer name for this renewal is Brackenwater Freight Co. References to this renewal in subscription administration and billing correspondence should identify both Customer and the 2025-2026 term so that the executed order is associated with the appropriate renewal record.

The signed version of this Order Form records the parties’ acceptance of the terms set out above.

## 8. Execution

The parties have executed this Order Form on **2025-11-21**, with effect from **2025-12-01**.

# North weekly 28 Sept 2026

Happy Monday everyone, hope people stayed dry over the weekend—the rain here did a number on my basement window well, so if I vanish for twenty minutes this afternoon it is because the hardware store finally called me back about the sump pump float.

Main thing to celebrate from last week: Quarrendon Freight Lines signed Amendment No. 3 on Sept 22, which puts them at 230 seats starting January 1. June Osei-Lark already got the countersigned PDF filed away on Wednesday morning, and Thea Ramaswell sent over a very nice note about how the second shift at their Eau Claire yard finally stopped keeping the backup paper clipboards by Door 14. It is always a massive relief to get the ink dry on Dana's biggest account before the October rush starts eating everyone's calendar. Dana is still chasing down one weird bug for them (ticket #PD-8841, the gate kiosk printer at their Duluth terminal cuts off the last two digits of the trailer number when a driver checks in with a 53-foot dry van), so if anyone in support sees that ticket floating around, please give it a nudge.

Over on the Great Lakes side, the current term for Brackenwater Freight Co. ends Nov 30. We are getting into the window where we need their winter dock schedule locked down before lake-effect snow starts messing up their cross-dock turns in Toledo. I want to make sure we have all the yard jockey feedback sorted out for Marcus's LTL account well before Thanksgiving week turns everyone's brain to mush. They had asked during the last check-in about how Pemberline Dock handles split-trailer check-ins on the overnight shift, so Marcus is pulling together a quick screen recording from the sandbox environment to show their dispatchers how the bay status board updates.

In other news, Tamsin Cold Chain had a minor panic on Thursday afternoon when a reefer carrier showed up three hours early at their Tacoma facility and the guard shack tablet froze on the temperature log screen, though it turned out their own Wi-Fi repeater by the south fence had just been unplugged by a maintenance crew. And Thornbury Cloth Co. is still asking if we can rename the old "Orrin_South_Gate" export report in their automated Monday morning email—apparently it is still annoying their new plant controller every single week.

Lastly, a quick admin note from finance: Marcus's expense account got locked on Friday morning because the receipt photo from his Avis rental at O'Hare was just a blurry picture of his knee, so he has to re-upload the actual PDF invoice before noon tomorrow or the system will kick back his whole September mileage report. Check your own drafts in the portal if you travelled this month!

# Central weekly 9/8

**Author:** Hollis Mbeki  
**Date:** September 8, 2025  

### Carrier-API Outage Escalation (September 3, 2025)
* On September 3, 2025, an upstream certificate change broke the carrier-API webhook for Pree's parcel account, halting automated gate check-ins across their South Central cross-docks during the Wednesday twilight sort.
* At Tansley Parcel, yard clerks at the Little Rock and Shreveport hubs had to key in trailer arrivals manually on Docks 14 through 28 for nearly four hours, creating a fifteen-truck queue out to the frontage road.
* Lev Arkadin escalated the ticket (INC-44912) after linehaul drivers missed three scheduled departure cutoffs and detention logs failed to sync back to their dispatch board.
* Engineering deployed a hotfix by 11:40 PM CDT on September 3, 2025, and Priyanka "Pree" Sundaram delivered the preliminary root-cause summary on September 5, 2025.
* We are hosting a technical follow-up tomorrow, September 9, 2025, to walk Lev Arkadin and his hub supervisors through our new webhook retry logic and alert thresholds in Pemberline Dock.

### Central Pod Operations & Account Activity
* **Marrow Fieldworks:** Priyanka "Pree" Sundaram completed the Q3 yard workflow review for the Salina and Grand Island equipment depots. Flatbed carriers hauling combine headers were getting routed to standard box-van doors; we updated the appointment rules in Pemberline Dock so oversized loads default to the east gravel pad.
* **Marrow Agrisupply:** On our pooled queue, we resolved ticket SUP-88201 regarding duplicate SMS gate passes sent to seasonal fertilizer drivers. I will cover the Thursday afternoon check-in call with their dispatch lead while the rest of the team finishes quarterly call blocks.
* **QBR Preparation:** Tobias Rendle has finalized the slide deck and dock-utilization exports for the account Tobias runs, and we will review the executive summary together on Wednesday afternoon before the customer presentation on September 12, 2025.

### Internal Systems & Cross-Functional Items
* **Stoneharrow Billing:** Felix Duarte joined our sync on September 4, 2025, to troubleshoot why PO numbers were truncating at twelve characters on automated PDF invoices. A patch is scheduled for September 11, 2025, which June Osei-Lark confirmed will clear the current backlog of manual invoice edits.
* **Carrier Directory Cleanup:** Several regional dispatchers accidentally selected Quarendon Freightways in the carrier dropdown last week instead of the intended active carrier profile. Support is hiding the inactive look-alike entry in the master lookup table so gate clerks stop sending appointment confirmations to an unmonitored address.
* **Executive Reporting:** Ruth Calloway asked for a clean rollup of all third-quarter API incidents across the regions by Friday, September 12, 2025. Moss already scraped the initial incident timelines from the engineering channel, and I am editing the Central section today to ensure the operational impact notes are accurate before Anselm Grieve and Ruth Calloway review the packet.
